title: Quick quiz: how a heat pump works
intro: Ten questions on the machine itself. Tap an answer to see why.

qs.q: How does a heat pump heat your home?
options: It moves heat from the outside air into the house
It burns a small amount of fuel very efficiently
It stores heat from summer and releases it in winter
qs.why: A heat pump uses a refrigerant loop to carry heat in from outside air (or the ground). Moving heat takes far less energy than making it.

qs.q: Can a heat pump heat a home when it is below freezing outside?
options: Yes, cold-climate models are built to keep heating well below freezing
No, they stop working at 0 degrees
Only if a furnace runs at the same time
qs.why: Cold-climate models are tested and rated for low temperatures. Always check the rated output at your coldest design temperature.

qs.q: What does 'cold-climate' on a heat pump mean?
options: The model is tested and rated to deliver heat at low outdoor temperatures
The model is sold only in the north
The model has a built-in gas burner
qs.why: It is a performance rating, not a sales region. Many rebate programs ask for a cold-climate model on a qualified list.

qs.q: For each unit of electricity it uses, a heat pump delivers about:
options: 2 to 4 units of heat
Exactly 1 unit of heat
Less than 1 unit of heat
qs.why: Because it moves heat instead of making it, a heat pump is often 200 to 400 percent efficient. Electric baseboards top out at 100 percent.

options: An outdoor unit joined by thin lines to wall-mounted indoor units
A furnace that skips the duct cleaning
A window air conditioner with a heat setting
qs.why: It needs no ductwork. Each indoor unit heats and cools the room it sits in, which suits homes without ducts.

qs.q: Can a heat pump also cool your home in summer?
options: Yes, it runs in reverse like an air conditioner
No, it only heats
Only if you add a second outdoor unit
qs.why: A reversing valve switches the direction of heat flow, so one system heats in winter and cools in summer.

qs.q: What should an installer use to size a heat pump?
options: A heat-loss calculation for your home
Only the square footage
The size of your old furnace
qs.why: Square footage misses insulation, windows and air leaks. A proper heat-loss calculation avoids a unit that is too big or too small.

qs.q: You see steam or frost on the outdoor unit in winter. What is usually happening?
options: A normal defrost cycle melting frost off the coil
A refrigerant leak
The unit is broken and needs replacing
qs.why: Frost builds on the outdoor coil in cold, damp air. The unit briefly reverses to melt it, then goes back to heating.

qs.q: About how long does a well-installed heat pump last?
options: About 15 years
About 3 years
About 50 years
qs.why: Fifteen years is a common figure, longer with regular filter cleaning and yearly checks.

qs.q: Why do some homes keep backup heat with a heat pump?
options: To cover the few coldest hours if the heat pump cannot keep up
Because heat pumps do not work in winter
Because the law requires a furnace
qs.why: Right-sized cold-climate units handle most winter days. A small backup is a choice for the coldest extremes, not a sign the heat pump fails.
